newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Continuing disappointing tax inflows for the state is beginning to cause serious concern in the government's ranks. First quarter figures have seen an increase of 8.0 percent against targets of 14.6 percent. Prime Minister Costas Simitis has called a government meeting on the issue for Tuesday next week.

--The General Confederation of Workers of Greece has said it may boycott social dialogue with the government and employers on changes to the job market. Yesterday, a government meeting decided that the national economy and labour ministries would present a united front on the issues.

--Intense investor interest on the Athens bourse powered the general price index forward 3.13 percent at yesterday's session. The new boost is attributed mainly to improved economic indicators and recent rate cuts.

--THE ASE's general price index broke the 1,4000 barrier for the first time since the bourse's crisis in February, with investor interest centred on banking and construction. The new levels are a breath away from the six-year high for the general price index set in February this year.
--Xiosbank's initial public offer later this month will see share prices set at 2,650 drachmas. Public subscription will begin April 15 for the bank's share capital increase.
--The finance ministry is examining a new rescheduling of a backlog of debts to the state in an effort to boost tax revenues, according to latest reports.

--Commercial banks are concerned about market developments and under pressure to draft a policy on interest rates, following calls from National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou for restraint in rate cuts.

--The course of deindustrialisation in the public sector will be the focus of discussions on Thursday at the inter-ministerial deindustrialisation committee. The meeting is expected to discuss a timetable for firms and organisations monitored by the national economy and development ministries.
--OTE, Greece telecoms organisation, is establishing a new subsidiary that will provide services to the shipping community from Piraeus, making the port the telecoms hub of the Mediterranean.
--The dollar and pound sterling gained against the drachma on markets yesterday with the dollar climbing an extra four drachmas to close at 269.360 drachmas.
--The national economy ministry is considering a change in the institutional framework governing insider trading, a senior ministry official says.
